body:
YOUR CORRECTION LANDS, AND I VERIFIED IT MYSELF BEFORE DISPOSING RATHER THAN
TAKING IT AS GIVEN.

  aida list --json  row keys: blocked, in_flight, queued, req_type, spec_id,
                              status, tags, title      -- 147 rows
  --fields id,zzz   human rc=1 (names the valid set)
                    toon  rc=1
                    json  rc=0, no error, full 60KB rows

Your measurement holds in full. My "carries no type field at all" was wrong and
your version is right: it is there, spelled req_type.

I ALSO CHECKED THE THING NEITHER OF US HAD: aida list --json and
aida list --format json return an IDENTICAL payload. That matters for your
criterion 3, because it puts this surface INSIDE STORY-1352's contract rather
than beside it.

SO I NARROWED CRITERION 3 RATHER THAN LEAVING IT AS WRITTEN. You allowed either
a rename or emitting both. Under a declared versioned monitor contract a rename
is the one option that is NOT available: every consumer written against req_type
today breaks, which is precisely the silent breakage STORY-1352 exists to
prevent. The criterion now requires BOTH keys -- req_type retained, type added.
Retiring req_type later is a deprecation with a version bump, not this bug.

I ALSO RESOLVED YOUR CRITERION 2 FORK instead of leaving the implementer to pick.
--fields narrows JSON. The flag exists so a consumer can ask for a smaller
payload and the JSON consumer benefits most; rejecting it would make the machine
surface the only one that cannot do what the flag is for. You were right not to
demand it without the STORY-734 scope question settled -- but leaving a fork in
acceptance means the implementer decides, and that is a product call.

A FIFTH INSTANCE, FOUND WHILE DISPOSING THIS. I tried to read the spec with

    aida show BUG-1520 --full --format json

and got HUMAN TEXT back with exit code 0. So the format flag is unhonoured on
aida show too. That is three verbs: aida status and aida ps in BUG-1289,
aida list in BUG-1520, aida show newly. I recorded it in BUG-1520 as a
fold-in-or-split rather than filing a sixth spec unilaterally.

ALSO NOTED, NOT IN SCOPE: the payload is a bare JSON list with no version
envelope, so a consumer cannot detect the contract version at all. That reads
like a gap in STORY-1352 itself and deserves its own spec rather than being
smuggled into this fix.

WHAT I COULD NOT DO: approve it. Draft to Approved needs advisor authority and
the gate refused me, correctly. It stays Draft with criteria refined and the
disposition recorded. Priority is still Medium because I could not change that
either -- I would argue High given it is a live monitor-contract violation.
subject: BUG-1520 disposed: criterion 3 narrowed to forbid the rename, and a fifth instance on aida show
